patch.value: The auditor shell-tokenised every shebang file, so a Node script failed the gate on a template literal

The auditor treated any file whose first line begins with a shebang as executable shell and tokenised it with a shell grammar. A shebang says a file executes; it does not say it executes as shell, so a Node or Python program was being put through a parser that cannot represent it.

That was harmless only while an unresolved command position was skipped. Once the scan began auditing what it cannot resolve, which is the property that closes the variable-routed publish bypasses, a TypeScript template literal read as an unresolved program followed by a literal word and failed the gate on a file that runs no shell at all.

Measured in pm-csv, the one repository consuming this auditor: with 2026.9.5 the gate passes; with 2026.9.6 it reports 5 failures, all in scripts/docstring-gate.ts, whose only occurrence of the word publish is inside a template literal. Reverting the pin makes it pass, so the regression is the release rather than the repository. Every one of the 21 fleet repositories carries at least one shebang file naming a non-shell interpreter, scripts/docstring-gate.ts being present in all of them, so this is a fleet-wide false failure rather than a corner case, and a false failure here blocks every release.

The scanner's domain is now bounded to what it can parse: a shebang makes a file shell only when it names a shell, sh bash dash zsh ksh mksh or ash, whether direct or through env, and env's own options are stepped over so a shebang of the form env -S bash -eu names bash rather than -S. Nothing real is lost. A shell script carrying an extension is still matched by the path patterns; what the shebang branch adds is the extensionless shell script, which is exactly what the interpreter set still admits. Finding a publish inside a Node program is a genuine and separate problem needing spawn-call recognition, and shell-tokenising TypeScript never solved it.

Fixing the interpreter check exposed a second defect in the same path, caught by the regression test rather than by reading. The helper feeding this check read only the first TWO BYTES of a file, which was sufficient while any shebang counted, but left the new check seeing only the marker and therefore rejecting every shebang, including genuine shell scripts. That is the fail-open direction: an extensionless shell script carrying an unattested publish would have stopped being scanned. The helper now reads the first line, capped at the kernel's own 256-byte shebang limit.

Verified by execution rather than by reading, at both layers. isExecutableSource answers correctly for 13 path and shebang combinations covering all three shebang forms present in the fleet plus direct interpreters, an env with options, a bare env and a truncated marker. End to end, the fixed auditor was packed as a tarball and installed into pm-csv, where the repository's own gate passes while all five original bypasses plus the wrapper-spawned case are still caught.

Bounded the scanner's domain: a shebang makes a file shell only when it names a shell (sh, bash, dash, zsh, ksh, mksh, ash), direct or through env with its options stepped over. Also fixed the first-line reader, which returned only two bytes and would otherwise have rejected every shebang including genuine shell scripts.
A Node script is not tokenised as shell, while an extensionless shell script carrying an unattested publish is still audited.
Every shebang file was tokenised as shell, so a TypeScript template literal read as an unresolved command position followed by a literal word and failed the gate in all 21 fleet repositories.
